newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty flat vs basket, seen trailing dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty flat vs basket, seen trailing dlr/mark.

text.p: The Polish zloty was flat at opening levels of -0.67/-0.77 percent from the currency basket in early, low volume trade and dealers said is would drift sideways for the rest of the day following dollar/mark moves.
They said any potential zloty swings would be a resuly of dollar/mark rate shifts, as the US currency was at around its eight-year highs of 1.88 to the German mark.
"The zloty is likely to remain range-bound and to follow dollar/mark movements," said Tomasz Nowakowski, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

At 0750 GMT the zloty was at 3.4880/00 against the dollar and at 1.8540/55 against the mark against opening's 3.4840/80 and 1.8520/60 respectively. Some dealers said, however, the shallow market was vulnerable to sudden changes, if large investors stepped in.
"Larger zloty speculative moves are not unlikely if large investors, either domestic or foreign, appear," Nowakowski said, adding foreign players were now absent form the market.
Dealers said foreigners may start buying the zloty in a week or two when they see that T-bill yields start to top out after the central bank's August 4 rate rise.
The central bank raised its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and its discount by 2.5 to 24.5 percent on Monday.
Dealers did not expect larger foreign capital inflows on the forex market until the September 21 parliamentary polls.
On the money market one-day rates eased about half a point to 22.80/23.10 percent for O/N and 23.00/23.30 for T/N.
Dealers expected the central bank to stage a reverse repo tender to increase the bank's benchmark 14-day rate by some 0.5 point to 23.5 percent.
